**Test image analysis:**
- Young soybean plant (V1-V2 stage) completely collapsed at the soil line
- Stem shows brown/necrotic tissue at the base
- All leaves and cotyledons are dead and shriveled (tan/brown)
- Sandy soil visible; no green tissue remaining on the affected plant
- Classic post-emergence damping-off pattern

**Reasoning:**
- The Pythium reference images show very early pre/post-emergence seedling rot (cotyledon stage, soft water-soaked tissue) — doesn't match this more advanced plant stage
- The test image shows a more developed plant with a firm, collapsed stem at the soil line — this is characteristic of **Rhizoctonia** root rot, which causes reddish-brown hypocotyl cankers leading to post-emergence damping-off at a more advanced seedling stage than Pythium
- Phytophthora typically shows a water-soaked brown stem lesion progressing upward, less likely given the dry sandy conditions
- The complete collapse of the young plant with visible stem necrosis at soil level is the hallmark of Rhizoctonia post-emergence damping-off
